topic.title: Model Serving and Inference Optimization — vLLM, batching, KV cache and quantization

outcomes: Explain tokenization, prefill, decode, streaming and the model-serving request lifecycle.

explanation.problem: Notebook inference does not solve multi-user serving. Production must coordinate GPU memory, prompt processing, decode, queueing, batching, streaming, fairness and overload behavior.
explanation.plainLanguage:
A serving engine is a traffic controller around a model. Tokenization turns text into token IDs. Prefill processes the prompt and creates key/value cache entries. Decode predicts one token at a time while reusing that cache. The server streams output while scheduling many active sequences.

Static batching waits for a fixed group and can make short requests wait for long ones. Continuous batching schedules at iteration boundaries: finished sequences leave and new sequences enter when capacity permits. This improves utilization but still needs fairness, queue caps and cancellation.

KV cache is a major concurrency budget. For a conventional decoder, approximate bytes per token = 2 × layers × KV heads × head dimension × bytes per element. Multiply by all cached tokens and active sequences. Grouped-query attention changes KV-head count. Paged allocation, prefix sharing and quantized cache can change actual use. Reserve memory for weights, activations, temporary buffers, CUDA graphs and fragmentation.

A 7B-parameter model at 16-bit weights needs about 14 GB decimal for raw weights; 4-bit raw weights need about 3.5 GB before scales, metadata and runtime overhead. Quantization does not guarantee faster inference: kernel support, hardware, batch shape and memory bandwidth matter. Compare output quality on representative evaluations.

Measure queue wait, TTFT, inter-token latency, end-to-end p50/p95/p99, input/output tokens per second, GPU utilization, allocated/reserved memory, OOMs, cancellations and rejections. Pin model, runtime, hardware, precision, prompt distribution, output cap, concurrency and warmup. A benchmark without workload metadata is not reproducible.

vLLM is a common high-throughput GPU serving choice with continuous batching and PagedAttention. TGI offers a production text-generation server with batching and streaming. Ollama is convenient for local model packaging and developer workflows. Confirm architecture, model license, quantization, GPU/driver compatibility, security patch cadence and observability before selection.

Bound request size, prompt/output tokens, active sequences, queue length and deadlines. Propagate cancellation and per-tenant quotas. When full, return clear retryable overload (for example HTTP 429 with Retry-After), not unbounded work that later crashes the process.
explanation.mentalModel: HTTP → auth and token validation → bounded admission → tokenizer → prefill → KV cache → continuous decode → streaming → release resources → metrics.
limitations: Memory formulas are estimates; runtime allocators, kernels and parallelism affect actual use.
Larger batches can improve throughput while worsening queue wait, TTFT and tail latency.
Quantization can reduce quality and may not accelerate unsupported kernels or hardware.
Benchmark comparisons require identical workload and hardware metadata.
The local simulator teaches queue trade-offs but cannot predict GPU kernel performance.
Client cancellation must release queued and active work safely.
explanation.everydayAnalogy: A GPU is a finite-capacity kitchen. Prefill prepares an order, decode plates tokens one by one, continuous batching lets the expediter insert new tickets as stations free up, and KV cache is limited counter space.
explanation.mathMadeSimple: For 32 layers, 8 KV heads, head dimension 128 and FP16 cache: 2 × 32 × 8 × 128 × 2 = 131,072 bytes = 128 KiB/token. A 4,096-token sequence uses about 512 MiB; eight need 4 GiB before weights and runtime reserve.
explanation.productionImpact: Publish workload-aware SLOs, bound memory and queue growth, protect tenant fairness, stream with cancellation, and choose model/precision/engine/hardware from repeatable benchmark evidence.

useCase.scenario: Serve a decoder-only model behind an authenticated streaming API. Estimate KV cache, enforce queue and token budgets, and benchmark fixed prompt fixtures without requiring GPU hardware or paid infrastructure.
constraints: Bound active sequences and waiting requests.
Reject excessive prompt and output token budgets before admission.
Reserve memory for weights and runtime overhead.

Label synthetic simulator values as proxies, not GPU measurements.

failures.name: Unbounded queue
failures.symptom: Queue wait and memory grow until timeouts cascade.
failures.rootCause: Requests are accepted without queue or token caps.
failures.recovery: Bound queue and token budgets; return retryable overload.
failures.regressionTest: Fill queue and assert next request is rejected.

failures.name: KV cache OOM
failures.symptom: GPU allocation fails as context or concurrency rises.
failures.rootCause: Cache estimate ignores layers, KV heads, precision or reserve.
failures.recovery: Calculate cache per token and reserve non-cache memory.

failures.name: Head-of-line blocking
failures.symptom: Short requests wait behind long prompts.
failures.rootCause: FIFO scheduling and fixed batches ignore request cost.
failures.recovery: Use continuous batching, deadlines and tenant fairness.
failures.regressionTest: Mixed short/long workload keeps bounded short-request wait.

failures.name: Cancellation leak
failures.symptom: GPU continues work after client disconnect.
failures.rootCause: Disconnect is not propagated to active sequence.
failures.recovery: Cancel engine work and release reservations in finally paths.
failures.regressionTest: Cancel during decode and assert active/cache returns to baseline.

failures.name: Quantization quality regression
failures.symptom: Lower-bit model fails task quality checks.
failures.rootCause: Precision approved using memory metrics alone.
failures.recovery: Run representative quality evaluation with latency and memory.
failures.regressionTest: Block promotion beyond declared quality tolerance.

failures.name: Misleading benchmark
failures.symptom: Tokens/sec cannot be reproduced and hides TTFT.
failures.rootCause: Workload, warmup, hardware and output caps omitted.
failures.recovery: Pin workload and report TTFT, ITL, p50/p95 and metadata.

guidedExercise.title: Reject overload without leaking capacity
guidedExercise.instructions: Implement active and queue limits. Rejected requests reserve nothing; cancellation releases resources exactly once.
guidedExercise.solutionCode:
def can_admit(active, queued, max_active, max_queue):
    if active < max_active: return 'accepted'
    if queued < max_queue: return 'queued'
    return 'rejected'
guidedExercise.unitTests:
assert can_admit(0,0,1,1) == 'accepted'
assert can_admit(1,0,1,1) == 'queued'
assert can_admit(1,1,1,1) == 'rejected'
